summary: The legal input length is capped at 10,000, and the scaling benchmark did not reject a correct quadratic list-prepending implementation. Matching worst-case output and input lower bounds directly certify the current solution's optimality.

optimality.argument: The sum can contain max(m,n) + 1 binary digits, so producing the result already requires Omega(max(m,n)) time in the worst case. The current solution advances one cursor through each input, performs constant work per binary column, and reverses a linear-size result buffer once, giving O(max(m,n)) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: Adding one to an all-one longer operand produces max(m,n) + 1 output digits, which alone requires linear time to construct.
Each input cursor decreases monotonically, one output bit is appended per column, and the completed buffer is reversed exactly once.
The source-fidelity-verified examples cover unequal lengths and a final carry; black-box real-test execution passed all five existing ordinary correctness checks.
